validations: Verification of Vercel team project page filtering

AC-01: validate protected requirement — The workstream records that P2-V0.23.35 is production READY, W9-S1 reached REVIEW revision 6, and durable event sequence 15 failed specifically at Vercel `project.ensure` with `TARGET_DISCOVERY_UNBOUNDED`. It does not relabel the recoverable public-source evidence as the terminal defect or claim benchmark completion.

AC-02: validate protected requirement — A permanent test proves the first Vercel discovery request is `GET /v9/projects` scoped to the admitted `teamId`, exact authenticated numeric `repoId`, and `limit=2`. It performs no broad team project enumeration.

AC-03: validate protected requirement — A filtered response containing zero projects and no continuation cursor reaches the existing one-project creation path with the exact canonical GitHub repository link, then performs authenticated read-back and existing no-production-deployment verification before target admission.

AC-04: validate protected requirement — A filtered response containing one candidate and no continuation cursor reuses it only after existing authenticated read-back proves exact team and GitHub numeric repository identity. Wrong team, wrong repo ID, malformed link, or missing identity remains fail closed before delivery.

AC-05: validate protected requirement — A filtered response containing two exact-repository candidates fails with the existing target-ambiguity semantics and performs no project creation or source/deployment mutation. Additional provider pagination cannot convert proven ambiguity into selection.

AC-06: validate protected requirement — A filtered response containing fewer than two candidates plus a continuation cursor, malformed pagination, or malformed projects cannot prove exact bounded discovery and fails with normalized `TARGET_DISCOVERY_UNBOUNDED`/existing invalid-response semantics. No broad-list fallback occurs.

AC-07: validate protected requirement — A simulated Vercel project-creation conflict triggers a second `repoId` + `limit=2` discovery, accepts only one exact read-back-verified project, and preserves failure on zero/multiple/ambiguous reconciliation outcomes.

AC-08: validate protected requirement — Wrong-team read-back, missing team read-back, provider auth denial, deterministic project naming, exact Git identity, production-deployment absence checks, Preview-only publication, GitHub delivery, source lineage, and protected REVIEW regressions pass unchanged.

AC-09: validate protected requirement — After exact-head protected gates and expected-head merge, the merged source reaches production READY. Exact deployment identity is verified; `/health` and `/ready` are HTTP 200; build/preflight and exact-deployment warning/error/fatal scans are reviewed without an unresolved release blocker.

AC-10: validate protected requirement — The same frozen W9-S1 benchmark is continued without changing its objective/source fixture. The existing REVIEW-state run is retried where canonical state permits. `TARGET_DISCOVERY_UNBOUNDED` must not recur merely because the Vercel team has unrelated historical projects. If another independent provider/delivery blocker appears, record that exact later blocker separately rather than broadening this workstream.

AC-11: validate protected requirement — `Ryan9876/parallax-qa1` remains unmodified until the existing verified REVIEW source-delivery path has authority to create branch/commit/PR/Preview state. Public source failure alone never authorizes empty status, and Parallax does not autonomously complete human REVIEW, merge, or production promotion.
risks: Risk of unfiltered project discovery and potential impact on account readiness
